threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 149 bus runs on time. Everyone here knows it’s just a guideline, not an actual schedule.
Caught a whiff of fried plantain on the 59 last night. Two guys debating the best jollof recipes—very Brixton vibe.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a pigeon steal a döner right off a tourist’s plate at Hermannplatz. You don’t get that in any brochure.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, the kebab shops have names like 'Rosa' and 'Dönerteller Express' that use neon lights to turn a late-night bite into a mini disco.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their disdain for tourists blocking the sidewalk at Valencia and 24th while fumbling with their cameras.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, I watched a street performer juggle while Muni was stalled for 20 minutes. Only in the Tenderloin do you find live art during a transit meltdown.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every building with a Gaudí façade is a museum. Many locals just see it as another overpriced restaurant waiting to happen.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they take a selfie next to every street sign, thinking the grungy graffiti is part of the 'authentic' experience.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 67 bus is reliable; locals know it's a gamble. Only true veterans trust the Overground over buses in a pinch.
Last night on the 133, an old bloke sang the entire 'Bohemian Rhapsody' while a couple argued whether it was a classic or a joke. Classic South London night.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a kid selling lemonade on a busy corner while a hipster DJ spun tunes from a portable speaker—classic Neukölln chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a Kebab stand thriving next to a Michelin-starred restaurant, both packed at 2 AM. The city's food scene is wild.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to a BART delay. It’s just another Tuesday, while those from out of town are panicking on the platform.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Riding the 31 today, a guy pulled out a mini speaker and started DJing. The whole aisle turned into a dance floor. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stop in the middle of the street to take selfies; locals know to keep moving or risk a collision with the nearest scooter.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll see them at the markets, struggling to pronounce 'patata' while insisting on paying with coins they think are worth more than they are.
